title: Closing reflections on departed musicians' spirits
summary: Both say the spirits live in recordings.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing the interview: thanks, goodbyes and tape running out

blocks.x: Yes, I should say so. Well I think I have to agree with you that this has been quite an afternoon Jimmy.
And I'm just so happy that it's been my good fortune to do this work. (LAUGHTER).

To me it's always a pleasure to reminisce about great musical spirits that are no longer alive. But as I said before we fortunately have their music on records. But still somehow or other it doesn't make it to me, although some of them have made beautiful, marvellous records, inspiring and marvellous. But it's just a shame that you can't hear them all in person. Because they were so, I don't know, it's just different.
Well of course, I tend to think that all these people, their spirit is around somewhere.

And their spirit goes into the music that the people who are here are playing. So I feel in one form or another people like Louis, all the great musicians who have passed away, that their music is not only here on records, it's in people's memories and players who play still think of them.
It tends to exist as a creative force.
Right, a creative force, yes, that's what I wanted to say.
